commit.message:
feat(types): align nullable wire fields with spec (T | null) (#655)

Harmonize types and runtime normalization for `<X|null>` wire fields
that were previously `T?` (undefined-flavored) or typed as required:

- `MintQuoteBolt12Response.amount`: `Amount?` → `Amount | null` (NUT-25)
- `SwapMethod.min_amount`, `max_amount`: `AmountLike` → `AmountLike | null`
  (NUT-04/05/25/XX — were previously typed as required, despite spec
  defining them as `<int|null>`)

Each field is normalized at the response boundary via `nullIfUndefined`,
so mints that omit these entirely (e.g. older Nutshell builds for
SwapMethod, or non-spec mints for the bolt12 amount) get coerced to
spec-faithful `null` rather than leaking `undefined` past the type guard.

Also removes the now-unused internal `undefinedIfNull` helper — its sole
call site was the old bolt12 amount path.

Consumer compatibility: code using `??`, optional chaining, or truthy
checks is unaffected. Code that compared `q.amount === undefined` on a
bolt12 mint quote response, or destructured `min_amount`/`max_amount`
with a default value, will need to switch to null-safe checks (`?? 0`,
`!= null`, truthy). Bolt12 adoption is still early enough that downstream
impact is small in practice.

commit.message:
fix(wallet): verify DLEQ on received proofs even without requireDleq (NUT-12) (#656)

* fix(wallet): verify DLEQ on received proofs even without requireDleq (NUT-12)

NUT-12 requires wallets to verify any DLEQ included on a received Proof. Previously
prepareSwapToReceive only ran the check when the caller passed `requireDleq: true`,
so a token whose proofs carried a DLEQ was accepted without verification by default.

- Add `verifyDleqIfPresent` helper: returns true when no DLEQ is present, otherwise
  delegates to `hasValidDleq`. Distinct from the stricter "must be present and valid"
  semantic of `hasValidDleq`.
- Harden `hasValidDleq` to catch crypto-layer throws (out-of-range scalar, bad point
  encoding) and return false, while still propagating the legitimate
  "Undefined key for amount" error.
- prepareSwapToReceive now always validates: `requireDleq: true` keeps the strict
  check; otherwise verify-if-present runs unconditionally.

* fix(wallet): guard mint-response paths against undefined sigs and add recovery hints

Convert opaque "undefined is not an object (in dleq)" TypeErrors into
informative throws when a mint response is sparse or a proof is missing,
and point each post-commit failure at the NUT-09 restore recovery path
so downstream SDK consumers know how to recover stuck funds.

* test(NUT12): cover undefined-signature guard in OutputData.toProof

commit.message:
fix(mint): coerce omitted payment_preimage and witness to null (#653)

Per NUT-23, MeltQuoteBolt11Response.payment_preimage is `<str | null>`,
and per NUT-07, ProofState.witness is also `<str | null>`. Both TS types
already declare `string | null`, but the runtime didn't normalize either
field — mints that omit them (very common pre-payment for preimage, and
for non-NUT-10 proofs for witness) leave the value as `undefined`,
silently breaking consumer checks like `payment_preimage === null`.

Apply the existing Postel-style `nullIfUndefined` helper to both fields:

- `normalizeMeltBoltFields` now coerces `payment_preimage` after the
  fee_reserve/request validation. Covers bolt11 and bolt12 (NUT-25's
  response aliases NUT-23).
- `check()` iterates the validated `states` array and coerces each
  `witness` field.

Tests added for both code paths in the existing MSW unit suites.

commit.message:
feat(wallet): add maxSpendableAfterFees primitive (#654)

Returns the largest spendable amount from a proof set after subtracting
the per-proof input fees the mint charges, and (optionally) a melt
quote's `fee_reserve`. Single step of a "melt all funds" iteration —
caller fetches a quote, calls this with the quote's fee_reserve, then
re-quotes for the returned amount until the result stabilises.

Clamps to Amount.zero() when fees exceed total, to keep callers
inside an iteration loop without underflow throws.

commit.message:
refactor(mint): cast wire values as AmountLike, not Amount, in normalizers (#652)

The `normalize*Fields` helpers in `Mint.ts` accept JSON-parsed values that
arrive as `number | bigint | string` (i.e. `AmountLike`) and feed them
through `Amount.from(...)`. Casting them `as Amount` made each call site
read as if Amount instances arrive on the wire — they don't. `as AmountLike`
honestly describes the input and would catch future drift if `Amount` ever
gains a field that wire data wouldn't satisfy.

No behaviour change.

commit.message:
fix(wallet): treat expiry: 0 as no-expiry in validateMintQuote (#648)

CDK emits expiry: 0 on mint quote responses to mean "no expiry"; the
spec defines expiry as <int|null> where null is "no expiry". cashu-ts
was reading 0 as a real Unix timestamp (epoch 1970) and rejecting all
such quotes as expired.

Treat 0 as the null case so wallets can mint against CDK without
hitting "Mint quote ... has expired" on quotes the mint considers
perpetually valid. Adds a unit test pinning the new behaviour.

Affects all mint methods (bolt11/bolt12/onchain) since validateMintQuote
is method-agnostic.

commit.message:
fix(mint): treat null amount on BOLT12 mint quote as no-amount (#649)

* fix(mint): treat null amount on BOLT12 mint quote as no-amount

Per NUT-25 the BOLT12 mint quote `amount` field is <int|null>; null
means an amountless offer. CDK emits explicit null on the wire.
normalizeMintQuoteBolt12Fields was checking `=== undefined` only, so
the call fell through to `Amount.from(null)` which throws
"Unsupported amount input type" — breaking every BOLT12 amountless
mint quote against CDK.

Treat null and undefined alike (Postel-style), matching the spec
intent and matching how other nullable wire fields are handled.
Adds a regression test pinning the new behaviour.

* refactor(utils): add nullIfUndefined/undefinedIfNull helpers
